title: National Disability Insurance Scheme Amendment (Participant Service Guarantee and Other Measures) Bill 2022
snippet: passed. National Disability Insurance Scheme. This bill would cut red tape and set clearer decision-making timelines for the National Disability Insurance Scheme. It would create a Participant Service Guarantee that puts into law how long key processes can take and how the Agency must engage with people. The bill also simplifies plan changes, clarifies eligibility for those with episodic impairments, and lets the Agency pay providers directly for participants.. People with disability who use the NDIS, along with their families and carers, are the main groups affected.

title: Fair Work Amendment (Same Job, Same Pay) Bill 2021
snippet: lapsed. (s) ALBANESE, Anthony, MP. This bill would change the Fair Work Act so that workers hired through labour hire companies must be paid at least as much as directly hired workers doing the same job. It would stop labour hire firms from undercutting pay rates set by enterprise agreements, which the government says has been used to cut costs and exploit workers. Small businesses with fewer than 15 employees or meeting a tax law definition would be exempt from the new rules.. Workers employed through labour hire companies, their host employers, and labour hire businesses.

title: Customs Amendment (Banning Goods Produced By Forced Labour) Bill 2021 [No. 2]
snippet: lapsed. (s) SHARKIE, Rebekha, MP. This bill would stop goods made with forced labour from entering Australia. It changes the Customs Act 1901 to treat such goods as prohibited imports, with penalties for bringing them in. The ban applies worldwide and does not target any specific country or region.. Importers of goods made with forced labour would be affected.

title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Assurance of Senate Counting) Bill 2021
snippet: passed. Special Minister of State. This bill would change the Electoral Act to make Senate vote counting more transparent and secure. It would require the Electoral Commissioner to arrange independent security and software assessments of the computer systems used to scan, store and count Senate votes before each election. From 1 January 2023, the software used to distribute preferences and elect candidates would be checked to ensure it follows the rules in section 273A of the Electoral Act.. The Electoral Commissioner and scrutineers are affected.

title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Voter Integrity) Bill 2021
snippet: lapsed. Special Minister of State. This bill would require voters to show identification before voting at any polling place. It would define acceptable ID types and let voters without ID use a declaration vote or have another enrolled person attest to their identity. The bill follows recommendations from reports on the 2013, 2016, and 2019 elections.. Voters, the Australian Electoral Commission, and polling staff.

title: Electoral Legislation Amendment (Contingency Measures) Bill 2021
snippet: passed. Special Minister of State. The bill would let the Electoral Commissioner change how elections are run when a federal emergency law is in force. The commissioner could alter limited parts of the Electoral Act through a legislative instrument, after notifying the prime minister and opposition leader and publishing the changes online. The power to suspend or adjourn polling would move from local presiding officers to the commissioner and could not be delegated, and the start of scrutiny in a division would be delayed if polling was suspended there.. The Australian Electoral Commission, the Electoral Commissioner, the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, voters, and polling place presiding officers.

title: Customs Amendment (Controlled Trials) Bill 2021
snippet: lapsed. Home Affairs. The bill would allow the Australian Border Force to run time-limited trials of new trade practices with approved businesses in a controlled setting. The Comptroller-General of Customs could make rules setting qualification criteria, trial periods, conditions and affected obligations under the Customs Act. Trials could cover imports, exports, depots, warehouses, electronic communications, agents and customs brokers, and tariff concession orders, but not prohibited imports or exports.. Entities that are legal persons, natural persons or partnerships approved to participate in controlled trials, and the Australian Border Force.
